title: Statistical Inference I
description: An introduction to statistical inference: populations, samples and sampling methods, the sampling distributions of the mean and of proportions, point and interval estimation and sample size, the principles of hypothesis testing, tests for means, proportions and variances, and simple regression and correlation. Built from the STA 121 lectures of Dr O.E. Olubusoye, Dr O.I. Shittu and Dr A.U. Chukwu.

topics.title: Population, Sampling and Sampling Methods
topics.summary: Sampling uses a small part of a population to make statements about the whole. The lecture separates census, population and sample, gives the reasons for sampling and the errors involved, and describes random and non-random sampling methods.
subtopics: Finite, infinite, real and hypothetical populations

topics.title: Sampling Distribution of the Mean
topics.summary: A statistic varies from sample to sample, and its distribution over all possible samples is its sampling distribution. The sample mean is centred on µ with standard error σ/√n, and by the central limit theorem it is close to normal for large samples.
subtopics: Sampling distributions and all possible samples
Centre: x̄ is unbiased for µ
Spread: σ/√n and the finite correction
Shape: normal populations and the central limit theorem

topics.title: Sampling Distribution of Proportions
topics.summary: When each unit is a success or a failure, the sample proportion p̂ = x/n estimates the population proportion. Its sampling distribution has mean p and standard error √(pq/n), and it is close to normal for large samples, as is the difference of two proportions.
subtopics: Mean and standard error of p̂
Normal approximation: n ≥ 30, np ≥ 5, n(1 − p) ≥ 5

topics.title: Estimation, Confidence Intervals and Sample Size
topics.summary: Estimation gives a point estimate of a parameter and a confidence interval around it. Good estimators are unbiased, consistent and efficient. The margin-of-error formula also tells us how large a sample must be for a required precision.
subtopics: Properties of estimators: unbiased, consistent, efficient
Interval for µ with σ known
Interval for µ with σ unknown and the t-distribution
Sample size for a mean and for a proportion

topics.title: Principles of Hypothesis Testing
topics.summary: A hypothesis test decides, from a sample, whether to reject a claim about a parameter. It uses a null and an alternative hypothesis, a significance level, a test statistic and a critical region, and it can make Type I or Type II errors.
subtopics: Statistical hypotheses: null and alternative, simple and composite
Test statistic and level of significance
Acceptance and rejection regions; critical values
Type I and Type II errors, power and the p-value

topics.title: Tests for Means, Proportions and Variances
topics.summary: Large samples use z tests for one mean, two means, one proportion and two proportions. Small samples with unknown σ use t tests, and a single variance is tested with the chi-square statistic.
subtopics: z test for the difference of two means
z test for two proportions with a pooled estimate

topics.title: Regression and Correlation
topics.summary: Regression studies how one variable depends on another and fits the least-squares line y = α + βx. Correlation measures the mutual linear association between two variables, with Pearson's r for measurements and Spearman's coefficient for ranks.
subtopics: Scatter diagrams: linear, non-linear and no association
The least-squares line and the regression coefficient
Spearman's rank correlation and tied ranks
